cash-on-cash-return.summary: Cash-on-cash return measures the annual cash flow produced by the cash invested. Use the simple mode when you already know both amounts, or build a first-year rental worksheet from purchase funding, income, costs and a fixed-rate loan. The headline worksheet yield is after a separate capital reserve allowance; it also reports the yield before that allowance and cap rate at purchase price so you can see why the figures differ.
cash-on-cash-return.scope: USD, pre-owner-income-tax cash yield. Simple mode uses a supplied annual total or a recurring monthly amount multiplied by 12. Rental mode assumes 12 immediately stabilized months with unchanged rent and costs, a purchase loan no greater than price, and other upfront costs funded with cash. Actual first-year scheduled P&I is deducted; loan payments stop at payoff, while entered other financing costs apply throughout the year. No property growth, sale, refinance, taxes, borrowing eligibility or investment-quality score. A capital allowance is deducted below NOI and principal paydown is not cash income.

examples.title: A $6,000 cash distribution on $60,000 invested
examples.inputs: Annual pre-tax cash flow after entered operating costs, debt and capital allowance $6,000; cash invested $60,000.
steps: Use the full-year cash-flow amount, not gross rent.
examples.answer: Cash yield is 10%; this is not a total return including appreciation or sale proceeds.

examples.title: Separate the purchase cash, debt and replacement reserve
examples.inputs: Purchase $200,000 with a $120,000 loan at 0% for a 20-year arithmetic example. Closing $4,000, initial repairs $6,000, no initial reserve. Rent $2,000/month, 5% vacancy, $600 monthly operating costs and $100 replacement reserve.
examples.answer: Cash-on-cash return after reserve is 9.3333%; before reserve it is 10.6667%. Cap rate at purchase price is 7.8%.

items.question: How do you calculate cash-on-cash return?
items.answer: Divide annual pre-income-tax cash flow by the cash invested and multiply by 100. For example, $6,000 divided by $60,000 is 10%. Cash flow must already deduct operating costs and debt payments; include any capital allowance consistently. The rental worksheet builds that cash-flow figure from your inputs.

items.question: What counts as cash invested in rental property?
items.answer: This worksheet adds the cash paid toward the purchase, cash-paid closing and loan fees, initial repairs and initial reserve funds. The purchase loan is not cash you contributed. Enter each cash cost once. Do not substitute property value or current equity for the acquisition cash basis without changing the meaning of the ratio.

items.question: Do mortgage payments affect cash-on-cash return?
items.answer: Yes. The worksheet deducts both scheduled principal and interest paid during the first 12 months. Only actual payments count when the loan pays off within that year. Principal repayment can build equity but is not cash paid to you. Add mortgage insurance or other financing payments separately if they are not already included.

queries: cash on cash return vs cap rate
items.question: How is cash-on-cash return different from cap rate?
items.answer: Cap rate uses property NOI divided by a stated property value. Here it uses the purchase price and NOI before the separate capital reserve. Cash-on-cash uses cash flow after debt and the reserve allowance divided by initial cash invested. Financing changes cash yield while leaving that cap-rate calculation unchanged.

items.question: Can cash-on-cash return be negative or infinite?
items.answer: Negative annual cash flow divided by positive invested cash produces a negative percentage. A cash basis that is negative or rounds to zero at cent precision has no defined cash yield here, even if cash flow is positive. The calculator displays not applicable rather than an infinite or misleading return.

queries: how to calculate annualized cash-on-cash return
items.question: Should I use monthly or annual cash flow?
items.answer: Use a full-year total for an annual cash yield. In Simple Cash Return, Monthly assumes the supplied amount repeats for all 12 months. It is not a way to annualize an irregular sale distribution or compound a partial-year percentage. The property worksheet calculates the first 12 months and shows annual cash flow divided by 12 as a monthly equivalent.

items.question: Are replacement reserves included in this return?
items.answer: The headline property cash yield subtracts the entered monthly capital reserve below NOI. A second yield before that deduction appears in the result breakdown. Initial reserve cash is part of your starting investment; the ongoing allowance is a separate period cash-flow provision. Avoid deducting the same ongoing cost in both operating expenses and the reserve field.

items.question: What is a good cash-on-cash return?
items.answer: There is no universal cutoff that makes a rental investment good. Compare the same cash basis and cost treatment, then examine vacancy, repair needs, financing risk, location and the reliability of your estimates. A large percentage can come from a small cash denominator or omitted costs. It does not establish safety or predict total return.

items.question: Does cash-on-cash return include appreciation, sale proceeds or tax benefits?
items.answer: This calculator does not add appreciation, sale proceeds, tax deductions or principal paydown to annual cash income. It is a cash-yield measure for one period, not total ROI, IRR or CAGR. Use the rental property tool for a holding-period and sale projection, and keep the assumptions consistent.

items.question: Can I export the cash-on-cash calculation to Excel?
items.answer: Yes. Download CSV for your inputs or cash investment breakdown. Rental mode also exports the first-year cash-flow reconciliation and rent sensitivity. The files open in spreadsheet software as values; they are not an editable Excel formula workbook. For a simple annual case, the spreadsheet formula is annual cash flow divided by cash invested, formatted as a percentage.

items.question: How should I handle cash returned by refinancing?
items.answer: A refinance changes debt and may change the cash basis. It is not recurring rental income. Use the BRRRR calculator to reconcile loan proceeds, old debt payoff, fees and cash remaining. A post-refinance yield on remaining cash is different from this worksheet’s initial-acquisition yield, so label the basis when comparing them.
